payload.message:
Gate 1 is blocked: the automated checks it depends on failed on a probe the driver ran AFTER FEAT-2026-0203/T01's attempt failed and its changes were reset.

Failing check(s) found by that probe:
  - tests: tests (signature: (failures=3,)
  - coverage: other (signature: no_gate_marker)
  - roadmap-link-gate: other (signature: ERROR: roadmap.md:1089: FEAT-2026-0203's detail section says… active.**' and keep any prose after it)

FEAT-2026-0203/T01 WAS dispatched and its attempt failed. The driver then reset the tree and re-ran the checks to ask whether the failure predated that attempt; the result above is what that probe found.

The failing check(s)' TRACKED input files are unchanged vs the integration branch (the diff below is the feature's own plan/scaffold files, not code the failing check(s) read):
git diff main...HEAD --stat:
.../GATE-01-REVIEW.md                              |  23 +++
 .../GATE-01.md                                     |  45 ++++++
 .../PLAN.baseline.json                             |  45 ++++++
 .../FEAT-2026-0203-http-status-regression/PLAN.md  | 155 +++++++++++++++++++++
 .../WU-01-walking-skeleton.md                      |  76 ++++++++++
 .../WU-02-shared-duration-grammar.md               |  71 ++++++++++
 .../WU-03-schema-and-lint.md                       |  69 +++++++++
 .../WU-04-adapter-regression-rule.md               |  67 +++++++++
 .../WU-05-derive-monitoring-and-rule.md            |  67 +++++++++
 .../WU-90-gate-1-close.md                          |  52 +++++++
 .../events.jsonl                                   |   1 +
 .specfuse/roadmap.md                               |   6 +-
 12 files changed, 676 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

What that comparison does NOT cover: untracked and gitignored paths. `git reset --hard` restores tracked files and leaves ignored ones in place, so a check that reads a build or output directory (`out/`, `target/`, generated-code trees, caches) can fail on state this feature's own failed attempt produced. The diff above cannot distinguish that from pre-existing breakage.

What to do next:
  1. Check for leftover untracked/ignored state from the reset attempt FIRST — it is the cheapest to rule out and the most likely cause. `git status --ignored --short` and `git clean -ndX` list what survived; if a listed path feeds a failing check, that is your answer.
  2. Only if the tree is clean of those is this pre-existing debt — confirm by running the failing check(s) on the integration branch in a fresh checkout before assuming it.
  3. If it was leftover state, remove it and re-run; FEAT-2026-0203/T01 is back at its previous attempt count and will be retried.

There is no way to proceed past this halt in this version. A waiver that lets a feature continue against a red baseline is future work tracked as FEAT-2026-0052; it does not exist yet.
